svg.title: Submission Run -- IMMEDIATE targets graded inline

g.text: Submission Run -- IMMEDIATE targets graded inline
The instructor owns this script. It invokes
her test suite, then invokes our AI phase as a
separate command. Ordering and error handling
Phase 1: functional testing. Her suite reports to us.
rejects an identifier not registered on this
assignment with a 4xx naming it and listing
the registered ones, and the library raises
rather than swallowing it. A typo must fail
the instructor's test run, never record an
[her marking logic decides this target needs feedback]
Under AUTOGRADER this call IS the decision.
Failures only, a subset, a superset, a
partial-credit threshold: all just code she
writes here. That is why no ON_FAILURE
Phase 2: the autograder script invokes the AI phase
[a registered target has no recorded outcome]
An error, not a silent skip. The message must
say the assignment is misconfigured and the
student need do nothing, because on
Gradescope the student sees it too.
The guard is checked even here. An instructor
or TA re-running the autograder later must not
Written BEFORE grading starts, and overwritten
after. Last write wins, so a container killed
mid-grading leaves the student with their test
results rather than a bare autograder error.
The tests already succeeded and are already in
the database; there is no reason to lose them
grading_mode is IMMEDIATE, so every task marked
ai_needed is graded here and now. Nothing is
deferred to a rerun and the guard is set below.
Why an IMMEDIATE grading fails, and whether
1. Rate limiting. Every submission for the
assignment uses ONE instructor API key, and
everyone submits in the last hour before
the deadline. A burst of concurrent
containers on one key makes 429 the
expected case, not an edge case.
mid-grading. LLM latency sits inside the
platform's fixed timeout, and rate limiting
makes latency worse, during the same spike.
5. Context overflow. A student submits an
enormous file and the prompt exceeds the
6. Model refuses, or returns output the
Note that 1 and 2 are CORRELATED WITH THE
DEADLINE. The failure rate is not uniform: it
spikes exactly when the most students are
affected. That is a sharper argument against
IMMEDIATE for large courses than latency
alone, and it is why OQ-15 matters.
